app.title: Soil Texture Triangle
app.summary: A person uploads a CSV of samples and checks a preview of the first rows. They map three columns to the sand, silt and clay fractions, then choose a classification scheme and a colour map, and can name a column to size the points by. The app puts each sample into a texture class and draws all samples on a ternary triangle over the class regions. The person downloads the table with a texture class column added.

task.text: Assign each sample a class from a standard scheme based on its three-part composition, see where the samples fall on a ternary diagram, and export the labelled table.

data.text: A table of samples, each with three percentage fractions that add up to 100, plus optional ID and other measurement columns. A fixed classification scheme defines its classes as polygons in composition space.
data.item: a sample with sand, silt and clay percentages

stage.text: classifying measured particle-size compositions after lab analysis, before reporting

mechanism.text: Each part of the page is gated on the one before: the upload has to be read, and the column mapping filled in with three distinct columns, before the settings and the plot appear. The chosen scheme drives both the point-in-polygon classification and the coloured class regions behind the ternary scatter. The classified table can then be previewed and downloaded.

field.text: soil texture classification on a ternary diagram in soil science

workflow.name: classify items into a fixed scheme by their composition and export the labels

steps.here: Upload a CSV and see a preview of its first rows. Nothing else appears until the file has been read.

steps.step: map the input columns onto the quantities the method needs
steps.here: Three dropdowns pick the clay, sand and silt columns. A warning names any that are still unset, and the three must be distinct. Values are converted to numbers and checked to lie between 0 and 100 and add up to about 100.

steps.step: choose the classification scheme and display options
steps.here: A texture system dropdown (USDA or HYPRES) shows the scheme's description. Other controls pick a colour map for the class regions and an optional column to size the points by.

steps.step: compute a value from the data
steps.here: Each sample is turned into a point in the triangle and given the first class polygon that contains it, or 'Unknown' if none does.

steps.step: look over every item at a glance
steps.here: A ternary triangle draws the scheme's class polygons, filled and named, with all samples plotted on top. Points are labelled by sample ID and can be sized by the chosen column.
Download a CSV of the classified table, which adds a texture class column, and preview its first rows.

distinctive: Every item is a composition of three fractions that must add up to 100 (within ±1), so it is plotted on a ternary triangle instead of x–y axes.
The classes are polygons in composition space, and classification is a point-in-polygon test. A point outside every polygon is labelled 'Unknown'.
Two standard schemes can be swapped on the same data, and each one redraws both the class regions and the labels.
An optional extra measured column scales the point sizes, adding a fourth variable to the triangle.

parts.title: Column mapping
parts.summary: Lets the person choose which uploaded columns hold clay, sand and silt. It blocks until all three are set and distinct, and checks that the values form valid compositions.
